articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Premier League clubs eye Alexander-Arnold amid Real Madrid uncertainty
articles.description: Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold is considering his future at the Bernabéu, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Man City monitoring his situation. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City are keeping an eye on the situation of Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold, while Barcelona and Bayern Munich are scouting Aston Villa attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid defender Trent Alexander-Arnold is considering his future at the Bernabéu, with Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester City monitoring his situation, according to TEAMtalk. The 27-year-old is frustrated with limited playing time under José Mourinho, having made just three LaLiga starts this season amid competition from Denzel Dumfries, while his former club Liverpool are looking for reinforcements at right back following Jeremie Frimpong's injury. Meanwhile, Madrid are closing in on an official announcement for a new one-year contract extension with 34-year-old goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, reports Fabrizio Romano.

- Barcelona and Bayern Munich are scouting Aston Villa attacking midfielder Johan Manzambi following his strong start to Premier League life, TEAMtalk reports. The 21-year-old, who moved to the club from SC Freiburg for around £60 million this summer, has two goals and two assists in four matches, with Bayern viewing him as a target to explore if uncertainty grows over Michael Olise's future.

- Manchester United, Arsenal and Newcastle United are exploring a move for Roma full back Wesley, according to Football Insider. The 23-year-old's ability to play on both flanks has attracted interest from Old Trafford, though Roma are expected to demand a fee of €60 million to complete a deal.

- Chelsea are in contact with the representatives of AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott ahead of a potential January approach, Fabrizio Romano reports. With the Cherries unable to reach an agreement on a contract extension with the 23-year-old, they could let him move during the winter window, though any deal is expected to require an offer of at least £100 million.

- Manchester United have made contact regarding Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha, with Liverpool also showing interest, according to TEAMtalk. The 26-year-old Germany international is viewed by the Reds as an alternative target to Bournemouth's Scott, who (as above) could move to Chelsea.

Other rumors

- Real Madrid have submitted an official offer to sign Manchester United youngster JJ Gabriel, with an immediate decision on his future expected. (Diario Sport)

- Liverpool and Bayern Munich are interested in Barcelona defender Gerard Martín. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool are tracking €55-million rated Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara with plans to sign a key midfield reinforcement in 2027. (Fabrizio Romano)

- Aston Villa are close to agreeing a new contract extension with attacking midfielder Emiliano Buendía until the summer of 2029. (Daily Mail)

articles.headline: Ayyoub Bouaddi, Carlos Baleba offer hope amidst gathering storms at Manchester United and Manchester City
articles.description: It's been a bruising start to the season for the two Manchester giants, as Manchester United's struggles to rediscover their form under Michael Carrick show little sign of abating, and Manchester City contend with the consequences of their guilty verdict.
articles.body:
It's been a bruising start to the season for the two Manchester giants, as Manchester United's struggles to rediscover their form under Michael Carrick show little sign of abating, and Manchester City contend with the consequences of their guilty verdict.

But, two young midfielders are offering contrasting visions of a brighter future for both heavyweights, with Ayyoub Bouaddi and Carlos Baleba offering compelling reasons for optimism in their first Premier League starts for their new clubs.

Both arrived as expensive transfers - Morocco's Bouaddi at £85m, Cameroon's Baleba at £65m -- and face considerable expectations.

Bouaddi is heralded as the successor to Rodri, competing with Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernández, while Baleba -- ostensibly a replacement for the experienced Casemiro -- must help Carrick establish a midfield identity that has long eluded United.

Baleba must find his place in Carrick's identity-building operation at United, and play his part in helping the club successfully undertake a much-needed rebuild, while Bouaddi must prove that he can fit into City's own specific Pep-inspired playing identity and on-field expectations.

For Carrick, himself one of the most accomplished midfield conductors in Premier League history, the arrival of Baleba could give him the tools needed to solve a longstanding problem for the Red Devils and give his attacking players a platform upon which to operate.

The 22-year-old's introduction to the United midfield has been delayed by an ankle ligament injury sustained before the season began, but after making his debut from the bench against Tottenham Hotspur on October 10, he made his first PL start for the Red Devils at Leeds United on Sunday.

It came at a difficult moment, with United taking only six points from their opening six league games, with criticism from the terraces and the studio intensifying as the promise of last season dissipates.

With United's recruitment strategy under renewed scrutiny, Baleba's strong showing came at just the right time, offering evidence that Wilcox's midfield overhaul could yet pay dividends.

Partnering another expensive recruit, Brazilian Andrey Santos, Baleba brought mobility, physicality and composure against a combative Leeds midfield.

Across 74 minutes, he completed 88 percent of his passes and made a series of vital defensive contributions. Beyond the raw numbers, Baleba injected dynamism into a midfield that had appeared ponderous and vulnerable against more physical opponents.

That was clear last weekend, when troubled 10-men Tottenham largely bossed the midfield at Old Trafford, but Baleba's presence changed the dynamic against Leeds.

His agility in tight spaces and ability for accelerating away out of pressure give opponents something to think about, give United options, and can allow them to change the momentum of a contest.

articles.headline: Mike Evans unable to finish 49ers' win, exits with Achilles soreness
articles.description: San Francisco wide receiver Mike Evans was unable to make it through Monday's night's 23-17 victory over Washington, leaving with a lingering bout of Achilles soreness that prevented the 49ers veteran from practicing Thursday, Friday and Saturday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Before playing in and then departing Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders because of a sore right Achilles, San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans let coach Kyle Shanahan know that even though he didn't practice all week, he was ready to play in the game.

That, apparently, gave Shanahan enough belief to allow Evans to suit up against the Commanders, albeit with one important caveat.

"It was a pretty close call in terms of that he wasn't able to go all week, but just talking to Mike, just something he has dealt with in the past in his career and he felt confident to be good today," Shanahan said. "That was the confidence he gave me, but we knew he might not be able to last."

Indeed, Evans was unable to make it through the game, leaving with what Shanahan described after the 23-17 win as the "same thing that was bothering him all week." Which is to say, a continued version of the Achilles soreness that prevented Evans from practicing Thursday, Friday or Saturday.

Asked whether Evans would need further testing or imaging on the Achilles, Shanahan said "I don't believe so" while noting that Evans has been dealing with Achilles tendonitis.

The question now becomes whether Evans will be available for Sunday's matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, which is the Niners' last game before their Week 8 bye.

"It's something that he's had before," Shanahan said. "It's something that bothered him throughout the week. When you have Achilles tendinitis like he does, it kind of is what it is. ... I hope he recovers throughout the week, but you don't think it's a long-term thing, but right now it ended up costing him two quarters and hopefully he'll be able to play next week, but if not, we'll have to have the rest of the group step up and hopefully get him healed up by after the bye week."

Evans sustained the injury with 1:10 left in the second quarter and the 49ers holding a 13-3 lead. On second-and-15 at Washington's 28, Niners quarterback Brock Purdy threw to Evans breaking inside for a gain of 16 yards.

After Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves touched him down, Evans stayed down on the field and began attempting to stretch his right leg. Niners medical personnel then ran to help up Evans, offering support as he slowly walked directly back to the locker room.

The 49ers initially said Evans was questionable to return but ruled him out early in the third quarter. Evans had three catches for 94 yards before exiting, and the Niners' offense had 303 yards and 20 points at halftime.

With San Francisco without Evans in the second half, Washington mounted a big comeback. San Francisco had three consecutive three-and-outs in the fourth quarter and managed only three points and 72 yards after halftime as Washington dialed up blitzes and dared the Niners' other wideouts to beat them.

articles.headline: Ugonna Onyenso thought his NBA dream was over -- then the Detroit Pistons called him up
articles.description: Detroit Pistons center Ugonna Onyenso was surprised to hear his name called out 53rd at the 2026 NBA Draft, having once believed his dream of making the league was over, but is now confident he can grow into the sizable shoes left by Isaiah Stewart.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons center Ugonna Onyenso was surprised to hear his name called out 53rd at the 2026 NBA Draft, having once believed his dream of making the league was over, but is now confident he can grow into the sizable shoes left by Isaiah Stewart.

Stewart was traded to the Memphis Grizzlies in a deal which saw the Pistons acquire three future second round Draft picks. Onyenso, who bounced back at Virginia Cavaliers following spells at Kentucky and Kansas State, is a potential long-term successor -- though the 22-year-old from Owerri, Nigeria, knows there is a long journey ahead.

When asked what he wants the Pistons fans to remember him by, Onyenso told ESPN: "I feel like my defense -- what I bring on the floor defensively -- because they lost a shot-blocker and I want them to know that I'm going to bring that shot-blocking ability back on defense for them too."

Although he added that he even hopes to one day surpass Stewart in that aspect of the game, Onyenso admitted: "The pace is the biggest difference [between the NBA and college basketball]. My blocked shots have got to be on a different timing and I'm still figuring that out.

"Getting rebounds, getting pick-and-rolls really fast - the little things like that - being able to do it at a higher pace requires getting in shape and conditioning myself more, but I'm getting there."

Onyenso is also still adjusting to being a full-time professional basketball player as opposed to a student athlete, but he is certainly not complaining.

Having been developed through the NBA Academy Africa and then Putnam Science Academy in Connecticut, Onyenso arrived at Kentucky in 2022 as a highly-rated prospect with international experience for D'Tigers.

After a modest freshman year, Onyenso's sophomore season was derailed by a foot injury. He transferred to Kansas State, hoping to restore his spark, but the 2024-25 season was arguably the least productive of his college career.

After averaging 2.8 points, 2.4 rebounds and 0.9 blocks across 24 games, only two of which were starts, Onyenso feared his NBA dream was over.

Instead, a year with Virginia put him back on the map as he averaged 6.5 points and 4.9 rebounds per game and made the ACC All-Defensive team.

He said: "After Kansas State, I thought I had no shot to get into the NBA anymore. When I left Kansas State, I thought I was going to go to a low-major D1 [college], but as God may have it, I was fortunate enough to go to Virginia. That was when I [regained] hope that I may have a chance.

"When my coaches let me shoot the ball, I was like: 'Ok, I have a real chance to get back on the [Draft] board. It's all about being patient for me and locked into the goal. [If I had not made it to the NBA], I would have probably gone overseas and played."

As Draft night approached, Onyenso still was uncertain whether his career would continue in the NBA or abroad - and believed that if he was to get drafted, it would be as the last pick.

articles.headline: Commanders' Terry McLaurin carted off with knee injury in MNF loss to 49ers
articles.description: Terry McLaurin was carted off the field with his left leg in an air cast after injuring his knee against the 49ers. He'll undergo additional testing Tuesday.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a knee injury in the first quarter of Monday night's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers that "could be significant," according to coach Dan Quinn.

McLaurin will undergo more testing Tuesday to determine the severity of the injury.

"There's fear," Quinn said of what the results might show.

McLaurin was carted off the field with an air cast on his left knee after he attempted to cut sharply to the outside while running a route on third-and-9 with 2:16 left in the quarter. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels was sacked on the play.

"He's a brother to me. It sucks," Daniels said. "You see how hard he works ... Praying for Terry. He's been there for me through a lot since I came into this league, the adverse times I went through last year and so far this year, and he's been right by my side. I love Terry and appreciate him a lot."

McLaurin caught a 27-yard pass on the Commanders' first drive, leading to a field goal. He is second on the team in receptions with 15 and has a team-high 230 yards receiving, with one touchdown.

McLaurin, 31, sat out Washington's Week 4 game against the Indianapolis Colts after injuring a hamstring two days earlier, but he returned the following week.

He sat out seven games in 2025, ending a streak of 72 consecutive games played. Before last season, he had been a consistent producer, with five consecutive 1,000-yard seasons, from 2020 to 2024.

The Commanders also lost defensive tackle Javon Kinlaw to a knee injury late in the first half, and he was ruled out for the game.

McLaurin signed a three-year contract extension prior to last season. He'll count $34 million against the salary cap in 2027 and $39.5 million in 2028. The Commanders could either restructure his contract after this season or release him with $25.5 million in dead cap room.

articles.headline: Stephen Jones says Brian Schottenheimer has full support of Cowboys' ownership
articles.description: Brian Schottenheimer has the full support of Cowboys ownership, Stephen Jones said Monday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.
articles.headlineJa: スティーブン・ジョーンズ、ブライアン・ショットハイマーはカウボーイズのオーナー陣から全面的な支持を得ていると語る
articles.descriptionJa: スティーブン・ジョーンズは月曜日、ダラスの「105.3 The Fan」にて、ブライアン・ショットハイマーはカウボーイズのオーナー陣から全面的な支持を得ていると語った。
articles.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Twenty-three games into his tenure as the Dallas Cowboys head coach, Brian Schottenheimer has a 9-13-1 record and the full support of ownership.

"Absolutely. There's not any question in Jerry's and I's mind," executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "He has the team. There's no question they want to go out there and execute and make things happen. "We feel really good ... about our coaching staff. We just have to continue to evolve and get to a point where we can win these football games."

The Cowboys are 2-4 after Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers, dropping two straight games. Next week they play the 2-4 Philadelphia Eagles on ESPN's "Monday Night Football," looking to avoid the second three-game losing streak in Schottenheimer's tenure.

Schottenheimer said he did not need the public show of support.

"I think at the end of the day, I'm focused on the process of turning this around for myself, the players," Schottenheimer said Monday. "Certainly not good enough. We're disappointed with where we're at. We know we need to play better. We know we can play better. And I think at the end of the day, we've got the right guys to do that."

The Cowboys have struggled defensively for the entire season, but the offense, where Schottenheimer serves as the playcaller, has been off the last two games. Dak Prescott has been intercepted four times. Their 29 points in the last two games is the fewest in a two-game span of starts made by Prescott since Weeks 5-6 of the 2024 season.

The Cowboys' running game is 30th in the NFL with 456 yards through six games. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were also kept in check by the Packers as Prescott averaged 4.8 yards per attempt.

"In terms of changes, no, we're going to get back to work and we'll figure it out," Schottenheimer said. "We have great trust in our offense. I'm not concerned about our offense. Again, last two weeks, the last two weeks. We own that. It is what it is. It's not been good enough, but we also have a history of being really explosive, really good. And we've done that not only last year, but in four of our games this year."

Asked if he would want his team to be angry or measured following the last two games, Schottenheimer said, "I always like guys that are angry."

"I'd say right now I'm pretty pissed off," he said, adding, "I think they're pissed off too."

Four of the Cowboys' next five opponents -- Philadelphia, Arizona, Indianapolis and Tennessee -- are a combined 7-17. On Nov. 15 they host the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers.

"We're ready for a win," Schottenheimer said.

It's not quite do or die, but it's not far off.

"I'll never not take accountability for the fact that we're 2-4," Schottenheimer said. "It's not what we planned on being. That's not where the standard of what we're trying to do is. articles.headline: Maddison scores in 'dream' return as Spurs get 1st EPL win of season
articles.description: An emotional James Maddison said it was like a "dream" to produce a goal and help Tottenham climb off the bottom of the Premier League with a 3-1 home win.
articles.headlineJa: マディソンが「夢のような」復帰戦でゴール、スパーズが今季EPL初勝利
articles.descriptionJa: 感極まったジェームズ・マディソンは、ゴールを決めてトッテナムの3-1でのホーム勝利に貢献し、プレミアリーグの最下位脱出を助けられたことは「夢のよう」だったと語った。
articles.body:
An emotional James Maddison said it was like a "dream" to produce a goal and help Tottenham climb off the bottom of the Premier League with a 3-1 home win -- their first of the season in the league -- over Coventry City on Monday.

Maddison marked his first start in 526 days after back-to-back knee injuries with a special strike in the 14th minute after he sent a first-time effort over Carl Rushworth before he marked it with a trademark darts celebration.

Spurs playmaker Maddison was the best player on the pitch during an even first half but Coventry levelled through Jack Rudoni only four minutes into the second period, sparking a frantic period.

Boss Roberto De Zerbi watched Omar Marmoush fire Tottenham back in front with 58 minutes played before Tosin Adarabioyo, Andy Robertson and Marmoush were forced off with issues, allowing Dejan Kulusevski to make his own comeback after 17 months of injury hell.

Kulusevski received a special ovation and minutes later Ben Davies ensured the Swedish attacker would celebrate his comeback with all three points when Davies' scuffed effort beat Rushworth to earn Spurs an overdue first league victory of the campaign.

Maddison, who only returned from anterior cruciate ligament damage last April, said after impressing against his hometown club: "I hoped [to start].

"I spoke to the gaffer about it this week and just feeling like the right moment for me to go back into the starting XI after a stop-start start to the season.

"I just wanted to play well, show my quality and show what the team's missed in the last 18 months, or whatever it is since my last start.

"The gaffer asked me to play and said he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side so hopefully I did that. And obviously a goal like that is always nice."

It was Maddison's first goal since his last start -- a 3-1 victory over Bodo/Glimt in the semifinals of the Europa League at the end of the 2024-25 season.

"They're the ones you dream of. Without going too deep into it, them dark days last year, recovering from the ACL, you dream of them moments, them goals and that is the light at the end of the tunnel," Maddison told Sky Sports.

"That is why I was a bit emotional and I felt really proud of Dejan Kulusevski as well because him coming back.

"I knew exactly that feeling of him stepping onto the pitch after that time out, but those moments and goals make it all worth it."

articles.headline: Kulusevski returns as Spurs get first Premier League win of season
articles.description: Tottenham Hotspur climbed off the bottom of the Premier League after James Maddison's superb 14th-minute opener inspired a 3-1 home win over Coventry City on Monday.
articles.body:
Tottenham climbed off the bottom of the Premier League after James Maddison's superb 14th-minute opener inspired a 3-1 home win over Coventry City on Monday.

It was a night to savour for both Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski, who made his first appearance in 526 days after a 17-month absence with a patella injury.

Roberto De Zerbi gave Maddison the nod against his boyhood club and Spurs' No. 10 responded with a stunning curled effort from 22 yards before Coventry levelled four minutes into the second half through Jack Rudoni.

Omar Marmoush responded with his first goal for Tottenham with 58 minutes played and after Kulusevski was introduced to thunderous applause, a nervy finale was avoided when long-serving defender Ben Davies watched his scuffed effort beat Carl Rushworth in stoppage time.

It ensured Spurs claimed a first top-flight win of the season at the seventh time of asking and only a fourth at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium since Kulusevski and Maddison were injured in May 2025.

Spurs started bottom and without four players from the 1-1 draw at Manchester United, but De Zerbi was boosted with Maddison able to make a first start in 536 days and Kulusevski included in the matchday squad after an equally torrid time out.

Yet the hosts almost went behind after 11 seconds, with Antonín Kinsky denying Brandon Thomas-Asante from a tight angle.

After a midweek trip to Marbella, Spurs started like they were still on the beach with Kinsky fortunate to save Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's cross before the same player had a shot deflected over by Micky van de Ven.

With De Zerbi's team requiring a spark, Maddison produced a moment to savour against his old club in the 14th minute.

Not long after a clever dummy, Maddison sent a curled first-time effort over Rushworth and into the top corner to put Tottenham ahead in the Premier League for the first time this season.

Maddison's trademark darts celebration followed before Dominic Solanke had the ball in the net, but it was quickly followed by the offside flag.

Coventry remained a threat with Sidiki Cherif thwarted by a Jan Paul van Hecke block, before Maddison had a shot headed clear and Solanke fired over.

There was still time for Thomas-Asante to get in behind Spurs' defence, only for Van de Ven to produce a superb last-ditch tackle to ensure it was 1-0 at the break.

Four minutes after half-time and Coventry levelled through Rudoni after a catalogue of errors by Tottenham.

Van Hecke firstly gave the ball away and set Coventry on the counter-attack before Rudoni's effort was blocked by Asante-Thomas. But Sandro Tonali and Tosin Adarabioyo reacted slowly and Coventry midfielder Rudoni's follow-up was too strong for the weak hand of Kinsky.

De Zerbi watched his team react well with Tonali sending two efforts over before Marmoush put a lacklustre first half behind him with a maiden Spurs goal.
